The survey combines wordlists elicited during 1998 fieldwork with lists reused from earlier Bhil\-country, Dhule, Garasia, Dungra Bhil and Ahirani studies\. Source lexical\-similarity category numbers are retained only in Notes and do not assert historical cognacy\. English annotations are separated from phonetic forms; two literal unmatched open brackets remain preserved and explicitly flagged as uncertain\. Table 8 provides locality and administrative metadata but no point coordinates, so the thirty dialect records intentionally leave coordinates blank rather than inventing proxies\.

language.name: Haryanvi
language.map_marker: <svg viewBox="-2 -2 32 32" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><circle cx="14" cy="14" r="13" fill="#FF6600" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/></svg>

references.source:
Jeff Webster\.
Sociolinguistic survey of haryanvi\.
Technical Report 2024\-011, SIL International, 2024\.
The survey was conducted from August to October 1991\. Section 4\.1\.1 explicitly defines the printed group numbers as phonological\-similarity judgments rather than cognate relationships; Jambu retains them only as source notes\. Seven same\-list cross\-references are resolved deterministically\. Typed audit notes preserve faint, unlabelled and clipped fragments without guessing them into installed forms\. The report names the six localities but gives no point coordinates, so dialect coordinates remain blank\.
URL: [https://www\.sil\.org/system/files/reapdata/39/32/25/39322561837182664281680018892812535354/JLSR2024\\\_011\.pdf](https://www.sil.org/system/files/reapdata/39/32/25/39322561837182664281680018892812535354/JLSR2024\_011.pdf)\.
references.progress: Appendix A.3, printed pages 21--34: 1,553 manually transcribed lexical variants from all 1,238 responsive cells in the six HRT, HJN, HFT, HNG, HTR and HLH Haryanvi lists. Twenty-one visibly blank target cells and one elicitation-only target cell are audit-only. The 840 BPL Braj/Haryanvi, PBG Baghati Pahari, HIN Hindustani and PUN Punjabi comparison cells are retained audit-only and are not manually transcribed
references.provenance: Official SIL publisher PDF downloaded 2026-08-28, SHA-256 53121a1b9803ba502092866080e3bdb35457bc6040dcc7f47da508eca1fef2e2; the PDF is not redistributed. Reproducible raster extraction, structural OCR evidence, frozen manual target-cell transcription, source-local importer, complete 2,100-cell audit and manifest are in data/other/forms/raw_data/sil_haryanvi_2024; installed rows are data/other/forms/20260828-sil-haryanvi.csv
references.locator: Appendix A.3, printed p. 32, item 166, HTR

language.name: Malvi
language.map_marker: <svg viewBox="-2 -2 32 32" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><circle cx="14" cy="14" r="13" fill="#6BCD00" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/></svg>

references.source:
Bijumon Varghese, Mathews John, and Nelson Samuel\.
The malvi\-speaking people of madhya pradesh and rajasthan: a sociolinguistic profile\.
SIL Electronic Survey Report 2009\-011, SIL International, Dallas, Texas, 9 2009\.
The report states that schwa, turned a, turned v and alpha are used interchangeably and assumes no phonemic distinction among them\. Source IPA remains in Original/Phonemic while a dedicated display profile applies Jambu conventions\. Lexical\-similarity category numbers and letters are retained only in Notes and do not assert historical cognacy\. Thirty\-four used legacy CIDs were resolved without OCR: thirty\-one from the report's own IPA chart and three from the official SAG\-IPA conversion table plus rendered\-page checks\. The Thillorkhurd extraction was independently compared to its later Unicode reprint in ESR 2012\-002, with 132 exact response matches across 126 concepts\. Printed source metadata provide localities and administrative units but no point coordinates, so the thirty dialect rows intentionally leave coordinates blank\.
URL: [http://www\-01\.sil\.org/silesr/2009/silesr2009\-011\.pdf](http://www-01.sil.org/silesr/2009/silesr2009-011.pdf)\.
references.progress: Appendix B, printed pages 59--177: 6,894 lexical responses from thirty Malvi target lists grouped by the source as Ujjaini, Rajwadi, Umadwadi, Sondhwadi, Gond-Malvi and Bhil-Malvi. Excludes 37 target cells printed as "By Name" rather than a lexical form, two Bhili and two Nimadi comparison lists, the Bhopali comparison list, the Hindi, Gujarati and Marathi standards, ten explicit no-entry control cells, and prompts 11 breast, 23 urine and 24 feces which the report says were disqualified and removed
references.provenance: The exact official publisher PDF was recovered through Internet Archive capture 20150930085157 because the legacy SIL URL no longer serves the file directly; PDF SHA-256 e67e314974ab10eb8244b08dba56d08d1ce8cbf16eaef1be022071d49032a2dd. The PDF is not redistributed. Reproducible font decoding, geometric extraction and checked snapshot are in data/other/forms/raw_data/sil_malvi_2009; complete per-record audit is data/other/forms/raw_data/20260828-sil-malvi-audit.csv; installed rows are data/other/forms/20260828-sil-malvi.csv
references.locator: Appendix B, printed p. 143, item 170, Rajwadi-Malvi-Lojithara

references.source:
Amy Kim, Seung Kim, Palash Roy Sangma, and Mridul Ahmad\.
The tripura of bangladesh: a sociolinguistic survey\.
SIL Electronic Survey Report 2011\-038, SIL International, 2011\.
One printed line lists a form together with every site that gave it, so a line stands for as many attestations as it carries site codes\. Parenthesised material marks affixes, which the report treated as optional when comparing; it is preserved here\. Verbs \(items 171–222\) were elicited in the present continuous for Kok Borok, as commands for Garo and as verbal nouns for Bangla\.
URL: [https://www\.silbangladesh\.org/resources/archives/41655](https://www.silbangladesh.org/resources/archives/41655)\.
references.progress: Appendix A.3, "Wordlists": every elicitation printed for the 306-item list across all twenty-four survey sites -- twenty Kok Borok villages, the three Garo wordlists (Abeng, Chibok and A'tong) and the standard Bangla list. Excludes the printed gaps marked "no entry", the lexical-similarity counting procedures (A.1), the wordlist notes (A.2) and the report's non-lexical appendices
references.provenance: Freely published SIL Electronic Survey Report; the publisher PDF is not redistributed. Downloaded from sil.org on 2026-08-26; PDF SHA-256 3a40dff97634fba2996fe81c9b54c9faa360f2b41a35f559ba4d10e102ca6a6a; reproducible extraction in data/other/forms/raw_data/sil_bracket_wordlists.py with the checked-in per-record audit data/other/forms/raw_data/20260826-sil-tripura-audit.csv; installed rows in data/other/forms/20260826-sil-tripura.csv
